items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: then he showed me how to do some exercises and things. And I started to play these tenths.

ctx.x: He was from Roanoke, Virginia. He was on the pudgy side; everybody called him "Fats" -- Fats Wright. But he was an excellent piano player in every respect. We were talking one day, and I was talking about Teddy Wilson and Art Tatum, and I was saying how these guys played these tenths. I said, "Boy, I sure wish I could play tenths." And Fats also played tenths himself. That's how the subject came up. Because I was listening to him play, and I was admiring them tenths.

Fats was the kind of a guy, if you didn't know him well, you'd think he was always mad at you. When I said something about the tenths, he said something to the effect, "What the hell is wrong with you? Why can't you play tenths?" I said, "My hand is not that large." He said, "Hell, your hand is bigger than mine!" I couldn't believe that, and he took his hand and put it up against mine, and actually my fingers were I guess a sixteenth of an inch longer than his. So right away, I said, "Well, how the hell do you do…
